punchline: Income, schooling and marriage each explained about 3 percent of well-being; genes explained up to 52.
thirty_sec: In 1996 Lykken and Tellegen studied several thousand twins: socioeconomic status, education, income, marital status and religious commitment each explained no more than about 3 percent of the variance in well-being, while 44 to 52 percent was associated with genes.
